newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary revises 1997 real wage rise up to 3-4 pct.
newsitem.headline: Hungary revises 1997 real wage rise up to 3-4 pct.

text.p: Hungary's real wages will probably rise by three to four percent in 1997, more than the targeted two percent but this would not lead to restrictions, the Finance Ministry said on Wednesday.
Deputy State Secretary Tamas Tetenyi told a news conference that in theory an excessive increase in real wages can boost imports and lead to interest rate hikes.
"But currently I do not see that there is such a danger," he said.
Hungary's average real wages rose 7.2 percent in the first four months of the year.
But the growth rate in both the public and the private sector was likely to drop later this year, Tetenyi said.

"In the public sector, we see the real wage rise in 1997 meeting target," he said. "In the private sector, the rise was larger than expected but this was partly due to seasonal factors and the pace has slowed compared with the beginning of the year."
He added that in the Interest Coordination Council, the government was negotiating with employees and employers to keep wage increases within reasonable levels.
Tetenyi said the government did not plan to restrict wages by increasing tax burdens on individuals in 1998.
